paper.title: Causal Bandits for Linear Structural Equation Models

settings.name_in_paper: Causal bandit for linear SEMs with soft interventions (frequentist)
unmapped: Arms are the 2^N subsets of nodes of a known DAG (soft interventions); each node has an observational and an interventional linear mechanism with unknown weights
Learner observes all node values X(t) after each intervention (richer than bandit feedback on reward only); reward is X_N
Learner knows the bound m on ||X|| and the weight-norm bound m_B (used in beta_T)
Noise terms independent, 1-sub-Gaussian and with bounded norm

settings.name_in_paper: Causal bandit for linear SEMs (Bayesian setting)
unmapped: Arms are the 2^N subsets of nodes of a known DAG (soft interventions); linear SEM mechanisms with unknown weights
Learner observes all node values X(t); reward is X_N
Prior supported on weight vectors of norm <= m_B (Assumption 2)

settings.name_in_paper: Causal bandit for linear SEMs (lower bound)
unmapped: Arms are the 2^N subsets of nodes of a known DAG (soft interventions); linear SEM mechanisms
Learner observes all node values X(t); reward is X_N
settings.definition_quote: We assume the noise terms have standard Gaussian distributions ... Given the pair (d,L), for any N ..., there exists a causal bandit instance with graph parameters (d,L,N) such that expected regret of any algorithm is at least c d^{L/2-2} sqrt(T).

symbols.m_B: bound on norm of weight columns
symbols.beta_T: confidence radius m_B + sqrt(2 log(2NT) + (d+1) log(1 + m^2 T/(d+1)))
symbols.L_path: length of longest directed path in the DAG
symbols.lambda_T: E[sum_t sqrt(lambda_max(V_{N,a_t}(t)) / (lambda_min(V_{N,a_t}(t)) min_i lambda_min(V_{i,a_t}(t))))], data-dependent term bounded in Theorem 3

tuning: beta_T = m_B + sqrt(2 log(2NT) + (d+1) log(1 + m^2 T/(d+1)))

source.label: th:regret_ucb_part1
source.quote: Under Assumption~\ref{assumption:boundedness}, the regret of \algonameUCB{} is bounded by \E[R(T)]\leq 2m + 2 (\beta_{T}+m_B)^{L+1} (d+1)^{\frac{L}{2}} \lambda_{T}, where we have set \beta_{T} = m_B + \sqrt{2\log(2NT)+(d+1)\log(1+m^2T/(d+1))} and \lambda_T = ...

results.notes: Expected regret defined as T mu* - E[sum X_N] = E[sum (mu* - mu_{a_t})], i.e., pseudo-regret. Bound contains data-dependent lambda_T; Theorem 3 bounds lambda_T < 4 g(tau)/sqrt(kappa_min) sqrt(NT) + ... = O~(sqrt(NT)) (not recorded separately as it is not a regret bound).

symbols.L_path: length of longest directed path in the DAG
symbols.N_nodes: number of nodes in the DAG (2^N interventions)

conditions: constants kappa_min, kappa_max, m, m_B hidden in O~

source.label: th:regret_ucb_final
source.quote: Under Assumption~\ref{assumption:boundedness}, the regret of LinSEM-UCB is \E[R(T)] = \tilde \mcO( d^{L+\frac{1}{2}} \sqrt{NT}).

results.notes: Combines Theorems 2 and 3. Hidden constants include 1/sqrt(kappa_min) (minimum singular value of parents' second-moment matrices over interventions).

symbols.L_path: length of longest directed path in the DAG
symbols.N_nodes: number of nodes in the DAG

source.label: th:regret_ts
source.quote: Under Assumption~\ref{assumption:boundedness} and Assumption~\ref{assumption:boundedness:prior}, the Bayesian regret of \algonameTS{} is {\rm BR}(T) = \tilde \mcO( d^{L+\frac{1}{2}} \sqrt{NT}).

results.notes: Paper states LinSEM-TS does not need m or T, hence anytime. Constants depend on kappa_min over the prior domain.

symbols.L_path: length of longest directed path in the DAG

conditions: hard instances: hierarchical block plus d-ary trees, standard Gaussian noise, edge weights b = 1/sqrt(d) so m_B = 1

source.label: th:lower-bound
source.quote: Given the pair $(d,L)$, for any $N \in \{d(L-1)+2, \dots, d^L+d(L-1)+1\}$, there exists a causal bandit instance with graph parameters $(d,L,N)$ such that expected regret of any algorithm is at least \E[R(T)] \geq c d^{\frac{L}{2}-2}\sqrt{T}, where $c > 0$ is a constant.

results.notes: Proof gives c = exp(-1)/(8 sqrt(2)). Minimax lower bound via two instances differing in one affine term (Bretagnolle-Huber).
